passage.title: Elephants
lines: An elephant that dies of natural causes lives about sixty-five years. Of course, an
elephant can perish from several "unnatural causes": hunters may kill it, most
likely for the valuable ivory in its tusks; diseases can spread through an entire
herd; or drought, and the lack of food that nearly always comes with
an inadequate supply of water, can kill it.
But if an elephant survives these disasters, it falls prey to old age in its mid-sixties. Around
this age, death is blamed on the loss of the last set of molars. When that final set of
teeth is gone, the elephant dies of malnutrition because it cannot get adequate
nourishment. In old age, elephants tend to seek out a final home where there is shade for comfort
from the sun and soft vegetation for cushioning; the bones of many old elephants have been found in
such places.
